pages.title: Architecture: the decision core, the effect executor, and replication
pages.purpose: Explain the clean-sheet three-tier split (celld-logic pure decision core via on_event, celld effect/adapter host, celld-ltx replication) and the single serial actor execution shape.
instructions: Establish responsibility and ownership boundaries between the crates; describe Event/Effect/State and the actor mailroom; document the deterministic-simulation seam and the __celld_domain_select macro rationale.

pages.title: Cells, scopes, and the lifecycle state machine
pages.purpose: Explain what a cell is (a named Durable Object with its own SQLite), the scope charset fence, and the full phase state machine from cold start to residency, dormancy, eviction, and takeover.
instructions: Focus on the lifecycle phases, the capacity/activation admission policy, phase census names, and the cell scope security charset.

pages.title: Ownership, fencing, durability, and the output gate
pages.purpose: Explain the RPO=0 durability contract: bucket conditional writes, ownership records and epochs, node leases and self-fencing, the output gate, fleet vs bucket durability proofs.
instructions: Ground the fencing argument (epoch prefixes, ack rule, ownership read) and the output gate in source; cover conditional-write dialects across S3/GCS/Azure.

pages.title: The V8 JS runtime: isolates, the input gate, alarms, and WebSockets
pages.purpose: Explain how celld embeds V8 and executes Wrangler bundles: isolate pools, blockConcurrencyWhile input gating, alarms and the wake index, WebSocket hibernation, and the V8 heap limit.
instructions: Document the JS host setup, isolate pool logic, input gate semantics, alarm reconcile/wake index key scheme, and WebSocket hibernation classification.

pages.title: LTX replication and the in-fleet node log
pages.purpose: Explain how each committed SQLite write becomes an LTX capture and replica object, L0-L9 compaction and bundles, and the fleet node-log tier (write-all/ack-all ensemble).
instructions: Describe the LTX format surface, checkpoint/takeover capture, per-epoch prefix layout, compaction levels, tiering, and the node-log recovery takeover gate.

pages.title: Reserved cells: D1, KV, Queues, Workflows, and cron
pages.purpose: Explain the runtime-supplied Durable Object classes that back D1 databases, KV namespaces, Queue brokers, Workflows, and cron triggers.
instructions: Focus on the reserved class naming, namespace keying, and the pure policy each backs (KV size split, queue lease generation, cron one-per-fleet arming).

pages.title: Change guides: representative maintenance tasks
pages.purpose: Focused how-to guides for safe changes: adding a Worker API surface, tuning durability/latency vars, adding a cell-backed feature, upgrading between releases.
instructions: Write practical, scoped change guides anchored to narrowest validation the repo supports.

pages.title: Deploying applications and adopting generations
pages.purpose: Explain the deployment contract: Wrangler config allowlist, manifests, deployment versions, the pointer and in-place generation adoption, cron arm, and reserved classes.
instructions: Cover the supported Wrangler keys/features, deploy->bucket object layout, version hashing, and how resident objects move across generations with force rules.

pages.title: Operating a fleet: CLI, diagnostics, and memory pressure
pages.purpose: Explain node startup, listener/advertise policy, the operator CLI (diagnose, cell, d1, kv, queue), graceful shutdown handoff, fleet readiness gating, and memory-pressure shedding.
instructions: Cover the CLI surface, shutdown/rollout protocol, readiness gate, pressure shedding thresholds and cgroup measurement, and the fleet drain token.

pages.title: The internal operator API and /state surface
pages.purpose: Explain the internal-listener operator routes (/state, /reload, /shutdown, /cell, /evict, /do, health), the HMAC-authenticated peer and runtime routes, and what /state reports.
instructions: Document each operator route, the unauthenticated vs HMAC-authenticated split, and the /state fields.

pages.title: Security and trust model
pages.purpose: Explain the security boundary: trusted application, private network, bucket credentials, listeners split, peer HMAC, cell scope and authority fences, and forwarded headers.
instructions: Ground the trust boundary and each protection in source: peer HMAC headers and replay protection, cell scope charset, authority/URL parsing fence, and body limits.

pages.title: Telemetry: traces and logs to the bucket or OTLP
pages.purpose: Explain the optional telemetry subsystem: how spans and console.log are recorded, Parquet bucket sink vs OTLP collector, configuration, and the DuckDB query workflow.
instructions: Cover OTEL configuration, sampling, the Parquet schema and partitioning, flush/compaction, and the DuckDB query path.

pages.title: Testing and the deterministic simulation
pages.purpose: Explain how celld protects its three promises: differential conformance vs workerd, exhaustive TLA+ model checking, deterministic simulation of the decision core, and live fleet fault injection.
instructions: Document the layered testing strategy and how a change is validated, including the conformance corpus flag and sim store seam.

pages.title: celld Quickstart
pages.purpose: Practical getting-started guide: install, run a local dev node, deploy an example, operate a two-node fleet, and orient the reader to the rest of the wiki.
instructions: House the benchmark-required practical quickstart. Use the README and examples to show a real path from install to a running local app and a fleet.
